$comment: The documented production environment set: every variable the production
bundle (dist/vercel-api.cjs) must have in order to finish module load.
This is the input to scripts/ci/boot-probe.mjs. It is NOT a list of every
variable the app reads at runtime — only those without which the process
cannot boot at all. Variables a feature needs once serving belong in
server/.env.example, not here.
The probe holds this list to two properties, so it cannot rot quietly:
sufficiency — the bundle boots with ONLY these set. A PR that makes the
app require a new variable fails until the variable is
added here, which is the review moment where somebody has
to also set it in Vercel.
necessity   — removing any one of these breaks the boot. Nobody can pad
the list to get CI green without the padding being caught.
Values are deliberately fake. The probe only proves the process starts; it
never connects to anything. Do not put a real secret in this file.
WHAT THIS CANNOT DO: it cannot verify Vercel actually has these set. See
the drift note in scripts/ci/boot-probe.mjs.
GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT (2026-09-11). It was here
because server/index.ts exited when it was missing — a startup guard that
gated on NODE_ENV, which Vercel sets for previews too, so every preview
deployment died at boot and served 500 on every route. The credential is
subsystem-scoped: only LISA's crisis classifier and the BigQuery retention
archive use it. It now fails at USE, so it is no longer load-bearing at
boot and the necessity check correctly refuses to let it sit in this list.
WHAT REPLACED THE ENFORCEMENT: nothing at boot, by owner ruling, and that
is the point — a missing tutor credential must not stop checkout. Its
absence is reported once at startup as a WARN with event
`credentials_absent` (component GCP), which is the signal to alert on.
Do not re-add it here to restore a boot check: the necessity property will
fail, and re-adding the exit it implies would restore the outage.
